findings.title: The worker never proves it scrubs the CURRENT message: removing scrubPastedReview at the worker seam kills no test, so pasted review text can reach the prompt and the fixed notice is never stored
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Not equivalent and not an unexecuted branch: line 168 runs on every claimed turn, and the mutant changes two observable behaviours. (1) `generateOperatorReply` receives the RAW owner message, so a pasted review reaches buildOperatorPrompt — the intake's stated behaviour is that it 'reaches the snapshot as [review text removed]'. (2) `scrubbed.scrubbed` is then always false, so the `server_notice` segment at AgentTurnWorker.ts:242-244 is never prepended and the stored reply loses the fixed sentence. Searched for an oracle and found none: render.test.ts proves scrubPastedReview as a pure function; snapshot.integration.test.ts proves the HISTORY re-scrub in context.ts:231 and calls buildOperatorPrompt with a hand-written literal; turn-get-route.test.ts asserts the notice from a PRE-SEEDED stored segment behind a mocked module. No test seeds review-shaped owner_text and drives handleAgentTurn.

findings.title: sameTurnPayload's owner_text arm is unexercised — the idempotency test passes on a conversationId that its own helper varies, and the test's comment that a re-introduced .trim() would break it is false
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Not equivalent: dropping the owner_text comparison turns a same-key/same-conversation POST with different text from `turn_key_conflict` into `existing`, returning the first turn's ids for a message the owner never sent. The case executes. The oracle is broken, not absent: `baseTurnInput` (turn-worker.integration.test.ts:96) mints `conversationId: randomUUID()` on every call, and the repeat at :688 overrides only clientTurnKey and text — so the 409 comes from the conversation_id arm, not the text arm. The comment at :687-688 ('A `.trim()` re-introduced anywhere would make this return `existing` instead') is therefore false as written. Fix: pass the same conversationId to the repeat call.

findings.title: getTurnForOwner's account_id predicate has no non-mocked test: the route suite named 'scoped by account' mocks the module, so removing the cross-tenant guard kills nothing
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Not equivalent: without the predicate the polled turn read returns another account's turn — its status, failure reason, stored reply segments, proposals and unsupported rows — through GET /api/operator/turns/:id, breaking invariant #8. The branch executes on every call. turn-get-route.test.ts:19 replaces @/lib/agents/operator/turns wholesale, so its "404 across accounts" arm is produced by `mockGetTurnForOwner.mockResolvedValue(null)` and proves only the route's null->404 mapping. Reverse import search found no other caller and no live-DB suite touching getTurnForOwner.

findings.title: createTurn's conversation-ownership re-read can lose its account_id predicate undetected — the promised 'conversation owned by another account' case is mock-driven
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Not equivalent: the module's own docblock (turns.ts:85-88) states the guard's purpose — a client-minted conversation id colliding with another account's row must be `conversation_not_found`, never an upsert into the caller's account. Without the predicate the ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING insert silently loses, the unscoped re-read finds the foreign row, and the turn is inserted against another account's conversation. The branch executes on every POST. turns-route.test.ts:31 mocks createTurn, so its assertion is `mockCreateTurn.mockResolvedValue({kind:'conversation_not_found'})`; no live-DB case in turn-worker.integration.test.ts seeds a foreign conversation.

findings.title: A proposal's before/after preview is never asserted end-to-end: swapping them survives, so the card can show the change as the current state and the current state as the change
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Not equivalent on this test's data: the seeded location has no tone and `toneProposal` sets 'warm and brief', so before and after genuinely differ. The branch executes for every proposal. before/after are the full effective voice state that the owner reads on the card and that Run B's Apply is specified to preview against, and nothing checks them: proposals.test.ts asserts insertProposals binds FIXTURE before/after values, and the live claim-race case reads only operation, status, location_id, contract_version and requires_confirmation off the stored row.

findings.title: worker/jobs/agent-turn/failed-hook.ts ships with zero covering tests — the whole BullMQ-exhaustion terminal transition (outbox fence ordering, isExhausted boundary, the swallowed checkpoint) is unmeasured
findings.reason: Uncovered change: 85 new production lines, no test file imports handleAgentTurnFailed. The ordering it encodes (markOutboxFailed CAS first, failTurnIfNonTerminal only on a win) is the same ordering the flag-off path has a test for, and the judge sibling it copies has its own hook tests.

findings.title: getConversationForOwner (134 lines: actor scoping, the no-turns branch, the effective-rules projection, the asOf contract) has no non-mocked test
findings.reason: Uncovered change: conversation-route.test.ts mocks @/lib/agents/operator/turns, so the promised case 'GET conversation returns the actor's most recent conversation and the summary reads with timestamps' asserts a fixture the route echoes. The `created_by_user_id` predicate at :624 — the only thing scoping the no-id read to the acting owner — is never executed under test.

findings.title: Fragile assertion: `expect(typeof status.value).toBe('number')` is a type-shaped proxy for the behaviour 'the materialized value is the metric the status_ref named'
findings.reason: Behavioural replacement: seed a known per-location pending count that differs from draftsWaiting and posted7d, then assert `value` equals the pending count. As written, materializeStatus (AgentTurnWorker.ts:317-330) could map pending_count to draftsWaiting and the assertion would still hold — the transcript would then display a permanently wrong number, since the value is frozen at fenced completion and never re-derived.

findings.title: Vacuous assertion: `expect(mockClaimTurn).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` can never fail, because @/lib/agents/operator/turns is never mocked in this suite
findings.reason: mockClaimTurn is hoisted at :14 but no vi.mock wires it to claimTurn, so the spy is unreachable by construction. It reads as coverage of 'no claim was taken' while proving nothing. The property itself IS covered by `expect(statements).toHaveLength(2)` at :80; the fix is to delete the line or mock the module.

It still passes for an empty reply and would fail on a rename that changed nothing. Behavioural replacement: assert every parsed segment's `type` is in the StoredSegment union.

findings.title: readPosted7d hardcodes INTERVAL '7 days' while the reported period comes from RECENT_COMPLETED_DAYS — changing the constant would silently mislabel the window
findings.reason: Latent, not a defect today (RECENT_COMPLETED_DAYS is 7). The stored status segment carries reportingPeriodDays from the constant while the count comes from the literal, so the two can disagree after a one-line edit.
